idea.idea: Using ChatGPT search prompts for wholesale competitor pricing research
idea.angle: How traders can analyze market trends and vendor pricing using structured AI search queries in 3 minutes instead of scrolling endless search pages.
idea.audience_problem: Wholesalers and traders waste time opening dozens of Google links to check competitor prices and supplier updates.

piece.hook_reason: It directly addresses the specific pain point of time wasted on manual research, which is a major bottleneck for small traders and wholesalers.

slides.title: Stop opening 20 tabs to check competitor pricing
slides.subtitle: Use structured AI search prompts to analyze market trends in three minutes.

slides.title: Why manual search fails
slides.body: Searching for wholesale rates across multiple supplier sites is slow. You often waste time filtering through irrelevant links and ads instead of finding direct pricing data.

slides.title: How to structure your search
slides.subtitle: Use specific prompts to get direct, actionable market data.
items: Define your product and specific market region clearly.
Ask the AI to compare pricing across known vendor types.
Request a summary of market trends rather than just links.
Verify specific claims by checking the provided source links.

slides.title: Search engine reality
slides.myth: AI will replace all traditional search engines.
slides.fact: ChatGPT currently processes one-fifth the search query volume of Google. It is a tool for synthesis, not a total replacement.

slides.title: Important limitations to remember
items: AI may route queries through different search engines.
Sponsored product images are now appearing in results.
Always verify critical price data against primary sources.
Ads do not necessarily impact search quality yet.

slides.title: Key takeaways for traders
items: Use AI to synthesize data, not just find links.
ChatGPT search volume is growing but remains secondary.
Watch for sponsored product placements in AI results.
Combine AI speed with your own manual verification.

piece.caption: Traders often spend hours jumping between supplier websites to monitor price fluctuations. By using structured prompts in AI search tools, you can pull market summaries faster than manual browsing. Note that OpenAI now includes sponsored product images in results, so always double-check the actual vendor site before making bulk purchase decisions. ChatGPT handles roughly 20% of Google's query volume, making it a useful secondary tool, but it does not replace the need for your own market expertise. ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI.
ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI.
Hayden Field Nov 3, 2026, 6:30 PM UTC Link
Hayden Field is The Verge’s senior AI reporter. An AI beat reporter for more than five years, her work has also appeared in CNBC, MIT Technology Review, Wired UK, and other outlets. In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.
Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.)
Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade. During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree. (OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in-house search index, although there is still some speculation that it routes some queries through Google.)
The news comes amid an ongoing search engine shake-up, as Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third-party sites and invests heavily in AI tools — not just AI Overview but also additional generative AI capabilities , including personalized search results with visualizations and charts. But as search queries increasingly route through OpenAI and other AI labs’ services, other companies are investing in the same types of AI-focused search experience, even if they call it something else: for OpenAI, it’s “Intelligent UI,” or creating a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response. “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” Fry said.
Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year. OpenAI has defended its ads in the past, and Fry told reporters they hadn’t produced a lasting backlash. “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” he said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.”
OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before.
“Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.
